title: Irish Regulator Cracks Down: Musk's X Ordered to Stop, Banned from Using AI Agents to Scrape Data for Training Grok

content_html:
Regulatory pressure on large AI models at the level of data collection and compliance is continuing to intensify. The Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) recently publicly confirmed that it has formally ordered social media giant X (formerly Twitter) to suspend the use of third-party data collected by AI agents to train its Grok AI system.

Regulators Step In: The Sequence from Autonomous Scraping to an Emergency Halt

It is understood that the core of this regulatory storm stems from an AI agent recently launched by X called Grok Bot. Since late October, the agent began scraping relevant third-party data on a large scale and gradually importing it into the backend to support the training and iteration of AI models.

However, this move quickly drew close scrutiny from EU data regulators. Dale Sunderland, a commissioner at the Irish Data Protection Commission, said in an interview that over the past few weeks the regulator had raised "significant concerns" about this data processing activity by X. Based on a strict review of user privacy and data compliance, the regulator explicitly required X to immediately suspend the data processing. Facing regulatory pressure, the social media giant owned by Musk formally confirmed to the regulator on Monday that it would comply with the suspension order.
